::: {#def-causal-model .theorem}
## Causal model

A causal model $\mathcal C$ of an [NPSEM](#def-npsem) $\mathcal M$ under a set of [intervention regimes](#def-intervention-regime) $\mathfrak G$ is $\mathcal M$ together with its [interventional NPSEMs](#def-interventional-npsem), with the error terms held equal:

$$
\mathcal{C} = \big(\mathcal{M},\ \{\mathcal M^{(\Gamma)}\}_{\Gamma \in \mathfrak G}\big), \qquad U^{(\Gamma)}_V = U_V \quad \text{for all } V \in \mathbf V,\ \Gamma \in \mathfrak G.
$$

Here $U_V$ is the error term of $V$ in $\mathcal M$ and $U^{(\Gamma)}_V$ the error term of the corresponding variable in $\mathcal M^{(\Gamma)}$.

$\mathcal C$ is an NPSEM describing the behaviour of $\mathbf V$ together with its counterfactuals. The variables $\mathbf V$ associated with $\mathcal M$ are called **observational variables**; the variables $\mathbf V^{(\Gamma)}$ associated with each $\mathcal M^{(\Gamma)}$ are called **counterfactual variables**, obtained by recursive substitution. A counterfactual under the static regime that sets $V$'s parents to the values $\mathbf{pa}_V$ is written $V^{(\mathbf{pa}_V)}$.
:::
